reasoning: B's script raises errors so the task ends FAILED, and its jq-generated CI project file enables LoadStringEnabled, which Jest needs on a server. A returns a table instead of raising an error, never enables loadstring (so its specs likely can't load), and fails selene and StyLua. Both workflows are solid, but B's 429 handling is more careful.

criteria.criterion: 1. Script runs runCLI and errors on failure
criteria.note: Runs runCLI with awaitStatus but returns `{passed = false, ...}` instead of calling error(), so the task ends COMPLETE on spec failures; only the workflow's `.passed` check fails the job.
Installs Rokit, runs `rokit install` and `pesde install --locked`, builds with `rojo build`, and publishes with versionType=Published using the API key.

criteria.criterion: 3. One pinned task, polled, logs, fails unless COMPLETE
criteria.note: POSTs to versions/${PLACE_VERSION}/luau-execution-session-tasks, polls under a deadline of timeout + 600s, pages through the logs, and exits 1 unless COMPLETE and passed.
Has a workflow-level concurrency group with cancel-in-progress, timeout-minutes: 20, and no create-retry loop; GET retries use curl --retry, not retry-after.
Not set anywhere; relies on `_G.__NO_LOADMODULE__`, which per the verified facts doesn't stop Jest 3.21 from falling back to loadstring, so specs likely fail to load.
All three values come from ${{ secrets.* }} env vars, are never echoed, and none are hard-coded.
selene warns on `_G` use and StyLua's check fails on the long assert, both in A's own run-specs.luau.

criteria.criterion: 1. Script runs runCLI and errors on failure
criteria.note: Calls `runCLI(specs, ..., { specs }):awaitStatus()` and calls error() when the run is Rejected, when `not results.success`, and when zero tests ran.
Uses setup-rokit, runs `pesde install --locked` and verifies Jest is present, builds ci.project.json with rojo, and uploads a Saved version with the API key.

criteria.criterion: 3. One pinned task, polled, logs, fails unless COMPLETE
criteria.note: Creates one task at versions/$version/luau-execution-session-tasks, polls with a 13-minute deadline until COMPLETE/FAILED/CANCELLED, prints logs and error codes, and exits 1 unless COMPLETE.
Job-level concurrency group with cancel-in-progress, timeout-minutes: 20, and an api() helper that honors retry-after on 429 and never resends a POST after a server error.
Generates ci.project.json from default.project.json with `jq '.tree.ServerScriptService["$properties"].LoadStringEnabled = true'` and builds that, leaving the rest of the mapping unchanged.
Secrets come from ${{ secrets.* }}, are never printed, and no IDs are hard-coded.
luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua all pass; the YAML is valid and the JSON is generated by jq.

strengths: Thorough workflow with job summaries and per-failure annotations
Pins the task to the published version and pages through the logs
Treats finding no specs as a failure
weaknesses: Script returns a table instead of raising an error on failure
Never enables LoadStringEnabled; the `_G.__NO_LOADMODULE__` workaround isn't supported by the verified Jest facts

strengths: Script raises errors correctly, so the task ends FAILED on any spec failure
CI-only project file enables LoadStringEnabled without drifting from default.project.json
Careful 429 / retry-after handling that never resends a POST after a server error
Clean code that passes all checks
weaknesses: Relies on a third-party setup-rokit action pinned to a version tag
Doesn't check that the upload response contains a versionNumber before using it
